## Description

A `Stack.Host` is integrated with a `Split.Column` only when it is the direct and only child of the column. In this scenario the secondary column renders a `ContainedModalProvider` with a `ContainedModalOverContent`, and the modal renders the stack. The column does not set `disableStackIntegration`. The stack has to be an ordinary nested stack: it is shown inside the modal, with its own navigation bar, and it navigates there.

It guards against the stack asking the column to take it over. The column does not take over a stack that is not its direct child, so such a stack would not be shown at all.

## Note

- The scenario has to be rendered as the root of the app: import `TestSplitStackV5InContainedModal` as `Example` in `apps/App.tsx`. The Split is a top-level navigator, and the tests menu would push the scenario onto a stack.
- On iOS 26 and newer the primary column floats over the secondary one, so the content of the secondary column and of the modal is centered in the window, partly under the primary column.

## Steps

### Baseline

1. Start the app with **TestSplitStackV5InContainedModal** as its root.

   - [ ] The primary column shows "Primary column".
   - [ ] The secondary column shows "Plain column" with the "Open modal" button.

2. Tap "Open modal".

   - [ ] The modal covers the content of the secondary column and shows the "Nested root" screen with the navigation bar of the stack, titled "Nested root".
   - [ ] The screen shows the "Close modal" button below "Push Nested pushed".
   - [ ] No error is logged.

3. Tap "Push Nested pushed".

   - [ ] "Nested pushed" is pushed inside the modal, with a back button in the navigation bar of the stack.

4. Tap "Pop".

   - [ ] The modal shows "Nested root" again.

---

### Closing the modal

1. Tap "Close modal".

   - [ ] The secondary column shows "Plain column" with the "Open modal" button again.
